audit.why: 49.02% over 153 games with diff EVEN / 6-10 ratings is coherent. Early belongs to Mel on range (her Q 950 and E 1000 vs Swain Q 750, E 850); Swain takes over from level 2-3 once Nevermove is online and again at 6.
audit.corrected: Kept EVEN. Level chart already agrees across both layers (Skill, Swain, Swain, Skill, Skill, Swain, Swain) so no atomic chart group was needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 phase described Demonic Ascension as a clean flip and ignored Golden Eclipse entirely — Mel's R is global (25000 range) and scales off Overwhelm stacks, so 6 is not a free win for Swain.
audit.why: Mel R text: strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of distance, extra damage per stack. Overwhelm stacks infinitely from any Mel ability or attack damage.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Golden Eclipse and tells the player to deny Overwhelm stacks before committing R.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full layer treated Solar Snare as the only interaction and never mentioned Rebuttal, which is the actual decisive mechanic. It also mis-genders Mel throughout ('his answer', 'his all-in').
audit.why: Rebuttal (W) reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker. Nevermove (E) carries the projectile flag — the outgoing wave is the reflectable object. Vision of Empire (W) has no projectile flag and lands from above, so it is safe into a held Rebuttal. Death's Hand (Q) bolts pierce and stack damage per bolt, so they only hurt at close range. Mirror audit (mel__swain) states the same reading from Mel's side: reflect target here is Nevermove; against Demonic Ascension the answer is spacing, not W.
audit.corrected: tldr / winCon / enemyWin / dosFull now state: bait Rebuttal wide, then E-root; Rebuttal reflects E, not W.

audit.whatIsWrong: Searing Brilliance's burst tell was absent. Every Mel ability cast loads three bonus projectiles (up to nine) onto her next auto-attack.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule autoreset-burst-tell; confirmed by enemyKit P text.
audit.corrected: phases[0].why now keys the level-1 trade to the post-cast auto wind-up rather than the cast itself.

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere in the Do's.
audit.why: Solar Snare is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s; Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s and is the far more punishable window. Vision of Empire is 22/21/20/19/18s.
audit.corrected: dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d now carry the concrete numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rebuttal carries a 'terrain — creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' derived flag, and the missing-interactions file builds a 'Mel cuts your retreat with Rebuttal, hold Flash for the wall' line on top of it.
audit.why: Riot's own W description says only that it forms a barrier around herself which reflects projectiles, prevents damage, and grants movement speed. Nothing about placed terrain. Per the brief's rule, the description beats the flag — so I did not write the retreat-cutting claim.
audit.corrected: Not written. Recorded here and in notes.

edits.before: Weather the poke — root his Solar Snare gap and drain the all-in. Swain wins the Solar Snare cooldown windows.
edits.after: Weather her volleys — E-root the Solar Snare gap and drain the all-in. Rebuttal reflects your E, not your W.

edits.before: Root his Solar Snare gap and drain the all-in. Track Solar Snare before every commit and keep the wave on your side.
edits.after: Bait Rebuttal wide, then E-root her step-up and drain. Track Solar Snare's 9s before every commit and hold the wave.

edits.before: Mel wins by landing Solar Snare, denying your pattern, and kiting you off the wave.
edits.after: Mel wins by rooting with Solar Snare, reflecting your E on Rebuttal, and kiting you off.

edits.before: W-poke and AA harass win the range war. Identify how Mel contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Any Mel ability loads bonus projectiles onto her next auto — the wind-up after a cast is your cue to step back.

edits.before: Demonic Ascension turns his all-in into your healing — bait it, then drain. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Mel's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension drains through her Q rotation, but Golden Eclipse hits from anywhere off Overwhelm stacks — deny stacks before you commit R.

edits.before: Her root / slow zone — sets up her combo. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Solar Snare roots at the centre and slows around it, down 9s at rank 5 — engage once it is gone.

edits.before: E-root Mel's step-up when his answer is down, right-click to drag the soul fragment, and Q the stacked wave-trade.
edits.after: E-root Mel's step-up once Rebuttal is down, right-click to pull her in, and stack Death's Hand bolts up close.

edits.before: Burning E on the wave — rootless Swain has no setup, and his all-in just became safe.
edits.after: Vision of Empire feeds your fragments — thrown blind it wastes an 18s cooldown.

notes: Rebuttal's derived 'terrain' flag contradicts Riot's description (barrier around herself, no placed wall). I trusted the description and did NOT write the missing-interactions 'Mel cuts your retreat with Rebuttal, hold Flash for the wall' line. Someone should verify in-game whether Rebuttal has any collision at all. Also: the full layer refers to Mel as 'he/his' in several fields I did not otherwise need to touch (ahead, breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, tradeBad, report[3].t, report[12].t) — a pronoun-only sweep would clean those up but each is a sub-10% change I left to a dedicated pass.
